title: ID0386436-DC/Si-D/SG-[MP / R4 170001684] XF3 to connect to WiFi
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
XF3 to connect to WiFi
Root cause: Dual Mobile APN visible in router
Solution: using command line, changed WAN 1, WAN 2 and WAN 3 as Ethernet, mobile and Wi-Fi
On DAMEX Sanctioned List: NO
Warranty Valid: Yes

additional_info.subject: Sicharge D XF3 to connect to WiFi
additional_info.body:
Dear Helpdesk
Product: Sicharge D
Serial Number: MP / R4 170001684
End Customer: Total Energies
Country: Singapore
XF3 connection: SIM Card
XF4 connection: LAN to external 4G (sim card) router
Problem statement:
Customer only want to use 1 SIM card which is on the external 4G router.
We would like to create a local hotspot on XF4 and request XF3 to connect to the WiFi hotspot of the XF4.
We are able to setup the hotspot on XF4.
Issue:
Upon checking XF3 on the WLAN option, we cannot find the WIFI option for WLAN
I am not sure if it is due to the router firmware or what.
Please kindly help

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0386436-DC/Si-D/SG-[MP / R4 170001684] XF3 to connect to WiFi CRM:00251000370
additional_info.body:
Hi Edna,
Here is the update.
Inserting SIM in one router (eitherXF4 or XF3) and creating hotspot out of it and connecting another router (XF3 or XF4) to it, can work.
However, please not this solution is not tested by R&D and reliability cannot be confirmed, especially because the changes have to be done by WebUI of the route and is someone changes other parameters or router settings by SCB, there is a risk that the configuration will be over written.
The best method is to have 2 individual SIM card in both routers, and let them run separately, however if customer is very reluctant about it, you can give it a try observe performance for some time.
Let me know, if you need further information.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Reetesh Sharma
